analysis: Reviewed docs/developer/build.md head text (lines 1-896). The patch only changes documentation: the "Last updated" date (line 3), CI runner-routing and job-size prose (lines 379-390, 492-496, 562-680), and CI cache/checkout prose (lines 697-719, 763-769, 796). No provider runtime, key custody, attestation, WebSocket, encryption or prefix-cache source is modified, so no threat-model asset (A-001..A-020) or boundary (TB-002/003/007/009/011/012/013/014) changes behavior. The cache-related text describes CI Actions caches, not the provider encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041), so T-041 posture (30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup tags, KEK purge) is unchanged. Security-relevant CI documentation: Darkbloom sandbox runners with no plane-granted cache set CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off so they do not write GitHub's Actions cache. Only pushes to master/dev and dev dispatches save caches, and PR caches are not seeded into master. A restored .git is deleted if it holds hooks, fsmonitor/hooksPath config, symlinks, or fails fsck. The documented design reduces cache-poisoning risk. Release and signing jobs keep literal Blacksmith labels. CI (master) restores only the strict-cache tier so released builds never reuse another recipe's objects. These claims describe workflows and scripts (scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, .github/workflows/*) that are not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that the docs match the implementation. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the range map is complete and the head text covers the changed regions. I found no concrete security regression or threat-model invalidation.
